conviction_note: The company's own June 25 guide ($40-50M sequential core EBITDA improvement) implies adjusted EPS near $2.05-2.15 against a $1.96 consensus that has drifted down 2% in 30 days, and scrap fell through the quarter while STLD confirmed metal-margin expansion for the overlapping period; but rebar imports from South Korea ran at 104kt in July (+85% y/y) against management's stated expectation that imports fall in H2, and this name sold its last two beats (-7.26% Oct 2025 on outlook, -4.69% Mar 2026), so the findings net to +0.8 while p_up sits at 53 on an abs move of 5.5 (option-implied ~8%, median history 3.56%).
bar: Adjusted EPS $1.96 on revenue $2.56B, nine estimates (AlphaStreet, https://news.alphastreet.com/commercial-metals-q4-2026-earnings-preview-october-15-street-expects-1-96-eps/ ; MarketBeat/Defense World $1.95-1.98, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-15-commercial-metals-stock/). Company guide from the Q3 call: core EBITDA up $40-50M q/q from $353.6M, NASG +~$40M, CSG mid-teens growth, Europe down ~$15-17M as the $20.4M CO2 credit does not recur (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026, 2026-06-25).
positioning_check: Short interest 6.31M shares, 5.74% of float, 9.37 days to cover per Fintel headline (settlement date not shown; latest listed settlement 2026-09-30), https://fintel.io/ss/us/cmc, up from 4.7M / 3.6 days at the 2026-07-15 settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/). FINRA off-exchange short volume ratio 53-76% daily 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-09 (same Fintel page). Not crowded; a modest build into the print. Options: baseline chain unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes, OI 495, P/C OI 0.39), so no skew; earnings-watcher.com quoted an options-implied move of about +/-8.0% as of 2026-09-27 (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/cmc-implied-move), against the baseline's 3.56% median realised reaction. Stock -4.9% over 30 days to Oct 9 (Simply Wall St), run-up 20d -0.64%.

findings.finding: US rebar imports were 112,306 mt in July 2026, +12.1% m/m and +84.6% y/y, with South Korea at 104,147 mt (5,071 mt in July 2025) and rising every month from April (69,751) through July; on the June 25 call management said imports were expected to go down in the second half and that South Korea was not competitive at current prices, and GMK/Kallanish report import availability limited US domestic rebar price rises at the start of September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: -7.26% on 2025-10-16 and -4.69% on 2026-03-26, both prints where the number was near consensus and the outlook/pricing commentary set the move; +3.94% on 2026-06-25 when management guided a sequential step-up.
findings.why_not_priced: The import series is a niche trade-press item published Sep 23, the same week the peer guides moved the group; if the market had priced a Korean import wave into CMC's FQ1 pricing, the consensus FY27 estimates and targets would have moved more than the -2% / $3 trims seen (JPM $86->$83 Sep 9), and the stock would not sit flat on 20 days at a 22% discount to its high with only 5.7% of float short.
findings.independence: GMK Center, 2 October 2026, citing Kallanish: import offers close to domestic prices after duties limited US domestic price increases in early September, https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-yamato-and-gerdau-have-raised-their-prices-for-beams-in-the-us/ . AISI: reinforcing bar imports +15% YTD through July 2026, https://www.steel.org/2026/08/aisi-releases-july-sima-imports-data-7/ .

findings.finding: Scrap costs eased through the fiscal fourth quarter (Fastmarkets settled changes: June flat, July -0.7%, August -0.8%, September ~flat) while the $30/short-ton rebar increase CMC led in early May 2026 (with a $20/t coil/bundle surcharge, followed by Nucor, Gerdau and Optimus) stayed in the market; Steel Dynamics' Sep 17 guide for the overlapping Jul-Sep quarter cites 'metal margin expansion across the platform and record shipments' with 'lower scrap costs', supporting CMC's guide to re-establish NASG metal margins ($610/t in Q3) and the ~$40M NASG sequential improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-06-25: adjusted EPS $1.73 vs $1.60 consensus with a sequential guide up, stock +3.94%. 2025-10-16: EPS beat ($1.37 vs $1.32) sold -7.26%. Beats on this line pay only when the forward margin commentary holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside the June guide, so mostly priced; the unpriced part is the direction of scrap through the quarter (down, where the Q3 call only said 'fairly stable') and STLD's independent confirmation on Sep 17. If fully priced the 30-day consensus revision would be up, not -2%.
findings.independence: Steel Dynamics Q3 2026 guidance 8-K ex99.1, 2026-09-17, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm ; GMK Center 6 May 2026 on the $30/st rebar increase, https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-gerdau-and-optimus-are-raising-rebar-prices-in-the-us/ ; Fastmarkets July and August outlooks, https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/us-scrap-trends-outlook-july-2026-2/ and https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/us-scrap-trends-outlook-august-2026/ .

findings.finding: Polish domestic rebar was assessed at 2,750-2,800 zloty/t CPT in the week to 25 September 2026 (about $724-737), versus 2,370-2,420 zloty/t in the same week of 2025 (+16% y/y), with mills pushing prices on rising energy costs while a distributor said demand remains weak and some mills adjusted working hours for energy prices; management guided Europe only +$3-5M operationally ex-CO2 credit, so Europe's Q4 EBITDA falls ~$15-17M q/q as the $20.4M credit does not recur, with the next tranche expected in FQ1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe has been a small segment ($34.7M adjusted EBITDA in Q3 vs $3.6M a year earlier); the baseline moves do not isolate it. The Q4 FY25 print carried a $30.7M CO2 credit and the stock fell 7.26% anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: The credit roll-off is in the guide and priced; the y/y Polish price level and the energy-cost pressure on FQ1 are not in any US preview. If priced, previews would mention Europe at all; AlphaStreet and MarketBeat do not.
findings.independence: Q3 call: three European price increases this year, metal margin +$37/t y/y, Polish electricity ~50% hedged, safeguard quota cut 50% with 50% tariff above quota from July 1 (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). Prior-year price level: Eurometal 9 September 2025, https://eurometal.net/?p=35322 .

findings.finding: Steel West Virginia start-up costs of $4-5M per quarter were guided to roughly double in Q4 before saleable product, hot commissioning had slipped from June to 'the later part of the summer' on ~100 days of weather delays, and the Aug 5 Investor Day deck describes completion 'by year-end 2026' and a ramp 'over the next 12 months', so the FY27 volume estimate of 250-300kt given in June is at risk of being trimmed on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Arizona 2's slow ramp was a recurring drag on prints in FY24-FY25; the Oct 2025 print (-7.26%) carried outlook disappointment. Start-up timing has moved this stock before.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 start-up cost is guided and priced; a further timing slip is not. If the market had priced a slip, FY27 estimates would have been cut more than the small trims recorded.
findings.independence: Q3 FY26 call, 2026-06-25: 'later part of the summer', ~100 days weather delays, FY27 250-300kt, https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026 . No third-party report of a first heat found in Aug-Sep 2026 searches.

findings.finding: On Aug 5, 2026 the board added $600M to the buyback, taking capacity to ~$717M (Q3 repurchases were only $18.9M), and management said repurchases return to a 'more elevated level' once net leverage is below 2x, with leverage at 2.1x at May 31 and 'clear visibility to <2x'; FY27 capex is guided ~$200M below FY26's ~$550M, so the Q4 repurchase figure and the FY27 capital-return cadence are live items on the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline turned on buyback pace; the Aug 5 announcement did not produce a visible move (stock drifted lower through August-September).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public and priced; the actual Q4 execution and whether leverage crossed 2x at Aug 31 are not. A priced-in acceleration would show as a firmer stock into the print rather than -4.9% over 30 days.
findings.independence: Q3 call on leverage and repurchase intent, https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026 ; 8-K Item 8.01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000119312526333797/d95091d8k.htm .

findings.finding: US nonresidential construction spending rose 0.7% in August 2026 to a 15-month high ($1,308.5B SAAR, data-centre-led; total spending +0.9% m/m, -1.7% y/y), while the Dodge Momentum Index was flat in August (282.0, -0.4% m/m, +4.2% y/y) with data-centre planning weakening and institutional planning +4.9%; the ABC backlog indicator was 8.8 months in June. Demand series for CMC's FQ4 (Jun-Aug) are steady rather than accelerating, consistent with but not above the 'healthy demand, strong backlogs' guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook commentary has set the sign on the last four prints in the baseline (two down, two up) more than the reported number.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public macro series and are priced as context; filed as a small proxy because the company has not spoken since June 25 and these are the only external reads on its quarter's demand.
findings.independence: Dodge Momentum Index August 2026 via Construction Dive, https://www.constructiondive.com/news/data-center-planning-august-dodge-momentum-index/829925/ ; ABC June backlog 8.8 months, https://www.abc.org/News-Media/News-Releases ; this is a macro proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 4.7M shares / 3.6 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 settlement to 6.31M shares / 5.74% of float / 9.37 days to cover in Fintel's latest headline (settlement not shown, latest listed 2026-09-30), with off-exchange short volume 53-76% of daily volume from Sep 28 to Oct 9; a modest short build into a print the company has guided up sequentially.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable in the baseline; 5.7% of float is not a crowded short by the 18-23% examples in the stage record.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price; filed so the judges see the size of the short and that it is modest, not as a thesis.
findings.independence: FINRA data via curvedtrading, 2026-07-15 settlement 4.7M / 3.58 days, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/ .

findings.finding: Management's own Q4 bridge ($40-50M sequential core EBITDA improvement on Q3's $353.6M, with the ~$60-65M per quarter purchase-accounting and interest gap unchanged for Q4 and a 7-9% tax rate) implies adjusted EPS of roughly $2.05-2.15 against the $1.96 consensus (nine estimates, down 2% in 30 days) and Q3's $1.73; the consensus sits below the low end of the company's own guided arithmetic after peers' Sep 17 guides missed and sell-side targets were trimmed (JPM $86->$83 on Sep 9; Investing.com lists Wells Fargo $80->$68 on 6/10/2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold beats: 2025-10-16 beat $1.37 vs $1.32 and fell 7.26%; 2026-03-26 fell 4.69%; the 2026-06-25 beat with a sequential guide rose 3.94%. Median absolute reaction 3.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the Street had the guide-implied number, consensus would be above $2.00 rather than drifting to $1.96; the drift followed peer guides (NUE -6.4% on Sep 18) rather than any CMC datum, and CMC does not pre-announce. Priced partly in the 30-day -4.9% slide.
findings.independence: AlphaStreet consensus, https://news.alphastreet.com/commercial-metals-q4-2026-earnings-preview-october-15-street-expects-1-96-eps/ ; Nucor Q3 guide and reaction, https://www.tikr.com/blog/nucor-stock-fell-6-4-on-a-guidance-miss-heres-where-shares-could-go-further ; Investing.com analyst table (date format ambiguous, read as 2026-10-06), https://au.investing.com/equities/commercial-metals-comp .

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias, the season's first major hurricane, made landfall on the northern Gulf Coast (Florida Panhandle / Alabama) around Oct 10-11, 2026 as a Category 2, inside CMC's Southeast precast and rebar footprint and five days before the call; a short-run disruption to FQ1 shipments is possible, with rebuild demand later.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weather was cited as a Q3 FY26 precast headwind ($52.9M precast EBITDA, project releases delayed ~two weeks in Georgia) and the stock still rose 3.94% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Too recent and too small for estimates; if it mattered to the quarter being reported it would be in the release, and it is not (FQ4 ended Aug 31). Filed small as an outlook-commentary risk.
findings.independence: NPR via KUOW, 2026-10-07, https://www.kuow.org/npr-news/2026-10-07/isaias-strengthens-into-the-first-hurricane-of-the-atlantic-season ; Ground News landfall aggregation (treated with caution).

findings.finding: Final US countervailing duties on rebar from Egypt (23.27%) and Vietnam (6.8%) were imposed in mid-September 2026 applying to shipments from Jan 13, 2026, following Algeria's 72.94% CVD (July 2) and 127.32% AD order (April 29); the trade framework management calls 'more durable' is firming, but the 2026 import surge is Korean, which these orders do not touch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff news has supported the group rather than moved CMC on print days; no print in the baseline turned on a duty order.
findings.why_not_priced: Known and small; filed because it is the counter-fact a judge would want beside the Korean import finding, and because the duties cover ~500kt of former supply that is not coming back.
findings.independence: Algeria CVD order via Law360 / Federal Register, https://policyrisk.com/federal-register/2026-08284 ; Investor Day deck on Section 232 and LTPF 2.0 pending, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000119312526333797/d95091dex992.htm .

baseline_tension: No skew is available (unusable chain) and the run-up is flat (-0.64% on 20 days, -22% from the 52-week high), so the findings neither confirm nor fight a market lean; they net slightly positive on the reported quarter and slightly negative on the FQ1 outlook, which matches a stock that has drifted lower with the peers since Sep 17 without a company datum of its own.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the guide-implied-EPS-above-consensus finding cut from +1.2 to +0.8 and the scrap/price finding from +1.0 to +0.8 because this name sold its Oct 2025 and Mar 2026 prints; p_up moved from 55 to 53.

Lesson 6 (inside the guide is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): Europe finding resolved from +0.3 to +0.1 since the credit roll-off and the $3-5M operational improvement are both guided; WV start-up cost finding kept at -0.4 only for the unguided slip risk.

Lesson 5 (narrow proxy below a company number): macro demand series trimmed from +0.3 to +0.2 and the Egypt/Vietnam duty finding from +0.2 to +0.1, both proxies the company has not confirmed for this quarter.
Lesson 7 (positioning before a negative): short interest checked (5.7% of float, rising); the Korean import negative trimmed from -1.5 to -1.3 for the modest short build, no further.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the Europe finding's two-sided text (prices +16% y/y vs weak demand) resolved into one near-zero size rather than left as a positive with a rebuttal.
Net: impact_sum moved from +1.6 to +0.8; abs_move_pct unchanged at 5.5; print_vs_bar unchanged at +4.
